name: Baccarat Punto Banco
description: Baccarat Punto Banco is the most prevalent version of Baccarat in modern casinos, particularly in Las Vegas and Macau. Unlike the original French variants where players make tactical decisions, Punto Banco is strictly mechanical. The dealer handles all cards according to fixed rules, making it a pure game of chance where the player's only choice is the initial wager.
origin: Havana, Cuba (later spread to Las Vegas and Macau)

history.origins: Developed in Havana, Cuba in the 1940s as a simplified, casino-banked version of Baccarat. It removed the rotating banker and player choices found in Chemin de Fer.
timeline: 1950s: Tommy Renzoni discovers the game in the Capri Casino, Havana.
1959: Renzoni introduces the game to the Dunes Hotel in Las Vegas.
1970s: Becomes the flagship 'high-limit' game for American casinos.
2000s: Explodes in popularity in Macau, becoming the world's highest-grossing casino game.
history.cultural: In Macau, the game is played with extreme intensity, often involving players squeezing the cards (peeking) before revealing them, even though the result is predetermined by the deal.
history.evolution: The transition from 'players banking each other' to 'house banking everyone' allowed the game to scale and be offered at much faster speeds.

setup.players: Up to 14 players at a 'Big Table' or 7 at a 'Mini' table.
setup.deck: 8 decks shuffled into a single shoe.
setup.dealing: Two cards are dealt face-up (or face-down to be squeezed) for 'Player' and 'Banker'.
setup.equipment: Baccarat table with Punto (Player) and Banco (Banker) betting areas, shoe, indicator markers, and scorecards (Roadmaps).

rules.objective: Predict which of the two hands (Player or Banker) will have a total closest to 9.
rules.gameplay: 1. Players place wagers on Player, Banker, or Tie. 2. Dealer deals two cards to Player and two to Banker. 3. If either has 8 or 9 (natural), both stand and hands are compared. 4. Otherwise: Player draws on 0-5, stands on 6-7. 5. Banker follows fixed Third Card Matrix based on Player's third card (if any). 6. Compare final totals; closest to 9 wins. Tie returns all wagers. Banker wins: 1:1 minus 5% commission.
keyRules: The Banker bet wins slightly more often than the Player bet.
Tie bets pay 8:1 (or 9:1 in some venues).
Winning Banker bets are subject to a 5% commission payable to the house.

strategy.basic: Bet on the Banker. Even with the 5% commission, it has a lower house edge (1.06%) compared to the Player bet (1.24%).
strategy.intermediate: Do not bet on the Tie. The Tie bet has a house edge of over 14%, which is mathematically disastrous over time.
strategy.advanced: Disregard 'Roadmaps' (patterns). While many players look for 'streaks' in scorecards (Big Eye Boy, Small Road), each hand is an independent event with nearly fixed odds.
tips: Avoid 'system' bets like Martingale; the house limits and the commission will erode your edge instantly.
If you want to play for longer, look for 'Commission-Free' Baccarat tables where Banker pays 1:1 except on a Banker win with 6 (which pays 1:2).

variations.name: Mini-Baccarat
variations.description: A faster, lower-limit version played on a standard blackjack-sized table where the dealer handles all cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Mini-Baccarat mainly changes table size and betting pace; core deal and third-card rules match the base game engine.

variations.name: Super 6 / No Commission
variations.description: Winning Banker bets pay 1:1 unless the Banker wins with a 6, which pays 50% of the bet.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Super 6 alters payout on specific Banker wins; payout tables are noted here but engine overrides are not yet parameterized.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the world's most popular baccarat variant. In Punto Banco, the house handles everything while you play the odds. Master the third-card matrix and learn why the Banker is the most strategic bet in the casino.
